DyMON is a novel approach for multi-view object-centric scene representation learning that is capable of learning from dynamic scenes and is able to disentangle the effects of object dynamics and camera motions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

i) we show that multi-view object-centric learning can be extended to dynamic scenes, ii) we introduce an approach that factorizes the effects of observer motions, scene object dynamics, and spatial ambiguities, and iii) we demonstrate that our learned object-centric representations are suitable for arbitrary space-time queries.
DyMON is the first method that learns object-centric scene representations from dynamic scenes, and it can support querying across both space and time.

DyMON is able to: i) factorize the entanglements between scene object dynamics and observer motions, and ii) learn to represent objects in a way that is independent of the observer motions and object dynamics.
